candidato.resumo: Antiresorptive drugs, which reduce bone breakdown, are an important part of treatment for breast cancer that has spread to the bones. However, their use can be associated with medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ), a condition in which bone tissue in the jaw dies. texto_fonte:
Jawbone necrosis in advanced breast cancer: Study highlights the importance of oral health
Antiresorptive drugs, which reduce bone breakdown, are an important part of treatment for breast cancer that has spread to the bones. However, their use can be associated with medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ), a condition in which bone tissue in the jaw dies. In a Finnish registry study, osteonecrosis of the jaw was diagnosed in 12.6% of patients treated with denosumab during long-term follow-up.
A nationwide registry study conducted by researchers at the University of Oulu has, for the first time in Finland, investigated how common medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw is among patients with breast cancer that has spread to the bones and which factors are associated with the condition. All patients included in the study were receiving antiresorptive treatment.
The paper is published in the journal Clinical Oral Investigations.
During follow-up, osteonecrosis of the jaw was diagnosed in 12.6% of patients treated with denosumab alone. Among patients who had initially received bisphosphonates before switching to denosumab, the corresponding figure was 15.3%. The condition was diagnosed in a small proportion of patients treated with bisphosphonates alone.
Antiresorptive drugs are used, among other purposes, to prevent skeletal complications caused by breast cancer that has spread to the bones. Osteonecrosis of the jaw is a recognized adverse effect of these medications, but its incidence among Finnish breast cancer patients had not previously been investigated.
Monitoring oral health is important
The study also found associations between dental procedures related to oral infections and osteonecrosis of the jaw. Tooth extraction and root canal treatment, in particular, were associated with a higher risk of the condition. However, the number of patients who underwent root canal treatment was small, and the finding does not establish that the procedure itself causes osteonecrosis of the jaw.
"The findings alone do not warrant changing or discontinuing antiresorptive treatment. Instead, the benefits and potential risks of treatment must be assessed on an individual basis. Nor should necessary dental treatment be withheld because of the associations observed," says Miika Kujanpää, a doctoral researcher at the University of Oulu.
"Our results highlight the importance of identifying and adequately treating potential sources of oral infection before starting antiresorptive therapy, as well as monitoring oral health throughout treatment. This requires close collaboration between oncology and oral health care professionals."
First Finnish population-based study on the topic
The study was conducted as a retrospective nationwide registry study, combining data from the Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL) and the Social Insurance Institution of Finland (Kela).
The study included 652 breast cancer patients with bone metastases who received antiresorptive treatment between 2013 and 2015. The patients were followed until the end of 2020.
The nationwide, population-based dataset made it possible to assess the incidence of medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw and the factors associated with it specifically among Finnish patients with breast cancer that had spread to the bones.
Further research needed on the impact of preventive dental care
According to the researchers, further studies should investigate in greater detail how drug dosage, treatment duration and cumulative exposure are associated with osteonecrosis of the jaw. More precise information is also needed on the timing of oral infections, dental procedures and the onset of osteonecrosis of the jaw to help distinguish the effects of different factors.
The researchers also emphasize the importance of sufficiently long follow-up. A long follow-up period of multiple years may be necessary, as osteonecrosis of the jaw can develop over an extended period and shorter follow-up may underestimate its incidence.
A particularly important research question is how much planned, preventive oral health care can reduce the risk of osteonecrosis of the jaw.
More information
Miika Kujanpää et al., Incidence and associated factors of medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw in breast cancer patients with bone metastases: a nationwide registry study in Finland, Clinical Oral Investigations (2026). DOI: 10.1007/s00784-026-07171-5

candidato.titulo: DNA analysis uncovers first known genetic connection between rare New Caledonian plant and parasitic plant
candidato.resumo: A new genetic analysis tool developed by UF assistant professor of biology Liming Cai, Ph.D., has led to the discovery of the first known interaction between Amborella, a rare New Caledonian plant, and a parasitic plant called Hachettea.

texto_fonte:
DNA analysis uncovers first known genetic connection between rare New Caledonian plant and parasitic plant
A new genetic analysis tool developed by UF assistant professor of biology Liming Cai, Ph.D., has led to the discovery of the first known interaction between Amborella, a rare New Caledonian plant, and a parasitic plant called Hachettea.
Cai and Rachel Cohen, Ph.D., a postdoctoral researcher in the biology department, made the discovery while developing a new method to identify horizontal gene transfer (HGT), the passing of genes between unrelated species, in plants. The tool, HGTScanner, found alien DNA in existing samples of Amborella, which represents the oldest surviving branch of flowering plants and is a rare shrub native to New Caledonia.
Cai said the fact that the interaction involved Amborella was enough to make the discovery notable because little is known about its life history despite its critical position in the evolutionary history of plants. But it also is the most significant finding that has come from her new horizontal gene transfer tool so far.
"The way people study ecological interactions, they would go to the field and then, either through observation or excavation, see who's interacting with whom," Cai said.
"When such interaction is so intense, these different parties can sometimes even exchange their genetic materials, and this is how our tool can be handy. We use a different approach to characterize species interaction in nature, not through direct field observation, but through the kind of genetic material that is being exchanged by different organisms."
Cai's discovery is part of a paper that was published in Methods in Ecology and Evolution. The interaction between Amborella and Hachettea was discovered while Cai and Cohen were testing their HGTScanner.
Cai said that, as a botanist, she is interested in the evolution and ecology of interactions between parasites and their hosts. But since there previously were no tools that could help identify HGT and pinpoint the donor and receiver, she was motivated to develop her own tool.
While HGTScanner itself is new, anyone could have used the DNA samples that led to this finding. She said she used a public DNA database to test her tool and picked Amborella because horizontal gene transfer is well documented in the plant. They found the alien DNA where they expected to find it, verifying the method while identifying novel transfers from Hachettea.
Cohen said being able to make this discovery with HGTScanner can have the same impact as making observations in the field. But the new tool allowed them to make this finding while saving time, money and resources for future fieldwork.
"In particular for parasitic plants, understanding who they're associated with, who they've associated with throughout their histories, can help us understand biodiversity at a greater scale," Cohen said, "and also maybe give us insight into who they might continue to parasitize and how that might work."
Using HGTScanner, Cai and Cohen discovered the gene transfer went from Hachettea to Amborella, the opposite of typical host-parasite gene transfer. And now, the team will look toward making a trip to New Caledonia to verify the ecological interaction.
Publication details
Liming Cai et al., HGTScanner : Detecting horizontal gene transfer at the fine scale using whole organelle genomes, Methods in Ecology and Evolution (2026). DOI: 10.1111/2041-210x.70419

candidato.titulo: Q&A: Mars Perseverance Rover Sets a Distance Record
candidato.resumo: On October 11 , the Perseverance rover completed a drive that brought its total distance traveled on Mars to 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers). This is a new record for Mars rovers, enabled in large part by Perseverance’s ability to drive with much more autonomy than its predecessors. Over the last five years, Perseverance’s autonomy software has been steadily upgraded, and to learn more about how the record was broken and what the future holds for the rover, we spoke with Mark Maimone , the Perseverance Robotic Operations Deputy Team Chief at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, who designed and developed the self-driving software for Mars rovers Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, and Perseverance. Before we talk about Perseverance, let’s pour one out for the previous record holder Opportunity , which landed on Mars in January of 2004 for a 3-month mission and ended its epic journey 15 years later in February of 2019. This NASA video compresses Opportunity’s entire mission into four minutes, and gives a poignant sense of the incredible distance that this little rover traveled over its 15 year life on Mars, doing science as it went: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory/YouTube Opportunity drove 4

texto_fonte:
On October 11, the Perseverance rover completed a drive that brought its total distance traveled on Mars to 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers). This is a new record for Mars rovers, enabled in large part by Perseverance’s ability to drive with much more autonomy than its predecessors. Over the last five years, Perseverance’s autonomy software has been steadily upgraded, and to learn more about how the record was broken and what the future holds for the rover, we spoke with Mark Maimone, the Perseverance Robotic Operations Deputy Team Chief at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, who designed and developed the self-driving software for Mars rovers Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, and Perseverance.
Before we talk about Perseverance, let’s pour one out for the previous record holder Opportunity, which landed on Mars in January of 2004 for a 3-month mission and ended its epic journey 15 years later in February of 2019. This NASA video compresses Opportunity’s entire mission into four minutes, and gives a poignant sense of the incredible distance that this little rover traveled over its 15 year life on Mars, doing science as it went:
Opportunity drove 45.16 kilometers until a planetary-scale dust storm stopped it in its tracks, appropriately enough, in Perseverance Valley.
On Feb. 18, 2021, Perseverance joined NASA’s Curiosity rover on the red planet, carrying the Ingenuity helicopter tucked under its belly. Curiosity and Perseverance both ditched Opportunity’s solar panels for a radioisotope thermoelectric generator. Curiosity has been active on Mars since 2012.
Despite Curiosity’s nearly 10 year head start, Perseverance is the rover to first break Opportunity’s record. There are several reasons for Perseverance overtaking Opportunity—ruggedized wheels for one—but the biggest contributor is that Perseverance was built for autonomy.
To understand how JPL taught a Mars rover to drive itself from 225 million kilometers away without crashing, IEEE Spectrum spoke with Mark Maimone, the Perseverance Robotic Operations Deputy Team Chief at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
Let’s talk about rover autonomy on Mars. Even before Perseverance, rovers were driving themselves, right?
Mark Maimone: Yes! Sojourner [in 1997] had an early kind of autonomous behavior—for sensing, it used four laser stripes projected onto the surface, which it used to measure the height of 20 points in the terrain in front of it. It could steer around big obstacles, or even thread the needle between two things. It was a real autonomy system, which is very impressive considering its CPU was less than one megahertz.
With Spirit and Opportunity, I developed the autonomy for those rovers. Every time they drove, they would use 256 x 256 pixel stereo pairs to map the geometry of the terrain and find a safe route forward. Spirit actually ended up driving itself 23% of the time, which I was frankly shocked by, since it drove much more slowly in that mode. But using autonomy helped Spirit travel 50% faster than it otherwise could have. Opportunity and Curiosity both only used autonomous driving about 5% of the time. Perseverance is the first Mars rover that drives itself 90% of the time, with its enhanced autonomy system that includes a second processor with an FPGA to do speed up extra image processing operations.
What was it like to let Perseverance drive itself for the first time?
Maimone: Perseverance is the culmination of decades of work on Mars rover autonomy, so seeing Perseverance use its AutoNav system to drive itself basically at full speed, up to 120 meters an hour, was incredible.
These two images taken by Perseverance’s hazard avoidance and navigation cameras show (on left) the very first AutoNav drive on Mars where the rover autonomously stopped before running into a rock pile, and (on right) the second AutoNav drive where the rover successfully steered around a rock.JPL-Caltech/NASA
Where are the humans in this process?
Maimone: The plan of where to go is specified by the science team, and then on the engineering side, the strategic route planning team develops a path to get us to that goal by guessing, based on lower-resolution maps from orbit, what the terrain is going to look like for the rover. Each day a tactical operations team combines the strategic overall route with that day’s science goals to pick the actual route the rover will follow.
We want humans to keep doing long-range planning because that avoids wasting time. For example, we’ve learned that if we see sandy areas with intersecting waves or crests—not just ripples blown in one direction, but cross-ripples going in multiple directions—the rover tends to sink into terrain like that, so we tell the rover to keep out of those areas. The onboard autonomy only measures terrain shape, not terrain type, so it benefits from those location-based annotations.
We now have years of experience correlating images taken from orbit with images taken by the rover, and understanding how different kinds of terrain affect the drive. With the current orbiters at Mars, we sometimes get 25 cm resolution on orbital images. That’s still not quite enough to see all obstacles; there could be a big rock that doesn’t really show up on a scale of more than one or two pixels, making it very hard to notice. That is why you want to have autonomy on the rover, but the greater help we can give it at a high level, the faster we can reach our goals and the fewer potential delays we’ll encounter.
This orbital view shows a region of complex Martian terrain that Perseverance could not navigate autonomously. The blue line shows the path that human planners estimated, while the white line shows the path taken by the rover. The inset image, from Perseverance’s hazard avoidance camera, shows the rocky, sandy, and sloped terrain.Source images: Olivier Toupet, Masahiro Ono, et al.; JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona/NASA
What happens when the autonomy system on Perseverance fails?
Maimone: We ended up not using the autonomy at all for about two months in more complex terrain while we tuned things and wrote new software to deal with that new terrain we hadn’t encountered before. Some of those changes were relatively quick, and some required months of study. For example, one parameter is the maximum amount of slope that the robot is allowed to climb, because on steep slopes, there is a risk of the rover slipping sideways.
We landed inside Jezero Crater, which was very flat, and so for the first three years most of our driving was at less than 14 degrees of slope. When we finally decided to leave the crater, we began to encounter other terrain at higher tilts with greater rock density, and the experience we gained allowed us to re-tune the parameters to allow the rover to traverse those more difficult terrains, with slopes of up to 24 degrees.
Rover autonomy in the age of AI
Late last year, you let Anthropic’s Claude AI plan a 400 meter drive for Perseverance. How did that go?
Maimone: We had the AI look at the orbital images and pick out a path for us, which became the starting point of the day’s rover planning operations. Typically, that starting path comes from the human rover planner team, but in this case, it was generated by AI. Humans were still in the loop; the team reviewed it, and made a couple of adjustments. AI gave us a solid starting point that allowed us to make rapid progress, because it’s much easier to validate a path than to pick one from scratch.
NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover took this selfie on July 23, 2024. The selfie is composed of 62 images taken by the WATSON (Wide Angle Topographic Sensor for Operations and eNgineering) camera on the end of the rover’s robotic arm.JPL-Caltech/MSSS/NASA
Do you think humans will remain a necessary part of rover operations, or do you see the next generation of Mars rovers operating for weeks at a time without human assistance?
Maimone: One of the things that has held us back from driving very long distances autonomously is that as we drive, the rover accumulates uncertainty in its position. When the uncertainty grows, it means we have to stay farther away from areas that human rover planners have identified as being potentially dangerous, called ‘keep-out zones.’ In some cases, the uncertainty gets high enough that the rover can’t plan a safe path, because the keep-out zones (which grow with the rover’s uncertainty) get too big.
We now have a new capability that we’ve added to Perseverance called Mars Global Localization. With this new technology that can shrink our uncertainty, we theoretically have the ability to go as long as we have resources to keep driving safely based on our maps and keep-out zones.
But to truly run a mission for weeks, you need to not only drive long distances, but also execute science operations autonomously. We have people here also looking at automating science operations by doing image processing onboard the rover to get a better understanding of what’s out there and where to focus the instruments’ attention. So I do think we are getting to the point where we can support long-period autonomous operations. It has been a slow evolution, but we have great capabilities now and a good understanding of what’s needed to make it work well.
As someone who has been involved with all of these Mars rovers—including one that got stuck—do you fundamentally trust Perseverance to operate autonomously?
Maimone: I do. We built the software, tested it, ran millions of simulations, and did lots of work in the field in many different test environments. It hasn’t steered us wrong yet. We’re looking forward to setting even bigger records.

texto_fonte:
On 12 October, Applied Materials unveiled a multibillion-dollar research facility in Sunnyvale, Calif., in the heart of Silicon Valley. The company first announced in 2023 plans to invest US $4 billion in its Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center, but now says it will invest even more: about $5 billion. The boost is part of a wider growth in private investment that is both enlarging the U.S. semiconductor R&D sector and making it more complex.
The EPIC announcement follows others, in August, by two semiconductor firms. Memory chipmaker Micron disclosed that it would invest $10 billion over 10 years at its Boise, Idaho, memory research lab, and SK Hynix said it will spend $4 billion on an advanced packaging facility in West Lafayette, Ind. (Neither of those companies responded to IEEE Spectrum’s questions about how much of those funds would be for R&D.)
The U.S. federal government has encouraged investment in U.S. semiconductor research by chip giants based in friendly nations, such as TSMC and Samsung. It has also enacted tariffs on foreign components and put some of its own money into faltering domestic chip companies including Intel. But the real motive behind today’s wave of private investment, according to some analysts and executives, is that companies anticipate enormous profits from feeding the current AI frenzy. “The best explanation is probably not about policy or politics and probably more about a big jump in revenue growth driven by AI demand,” says Chris Miller of Tufts University, and author of the book Chip War.
AI Money, Tools Accelerate Chipmaking
Applied Materials’ chief strategy officer Tristan Holtam agrees: “It’s really all about AI.” The firm estimates that the top 10 semiconductor companies’ revenue has grown about 150 percent since 2021 thanks to AI demand, and they have in turn raised their investment in R&D by 67 percent, he says. Those top semiconductor companies are collectively investing $67 billion this year in R&D, Holtam adds, dwarfing federal funding. Most of that federal money comes from the 2022 CHIPS and Science Act, which allocated $11 billion for R&D over several years.
While demand for AI-ready chips provides funding and motivation for more chip R&D, AI in the form of research tools is helping the people actually doing the R&D. Entegris, a semiconductor materials science company headquartered in Billerica, Mass., is applying AI in its early-stage research and design, says Olivier Blachier, the company’s chief innovation officer. At his company, workers are defining performance goals for next-generation products and asking AI tools to suggest promising new materials to match. “If you’re an AI engineer, a chemist, a materials scientist, you can combine scientific understanding with AI-driven modeling and simulation to work backward from a target performance requirement,” he says. The company is also piloting AI for preliminary screening of potential new materials, similar to what the pharmaceutical industry does with new molecules before trying to synthesize and evaluate materials in the lab.
At Applied Materials, Holtam reports that the company is making use of AI-enabled acceleration in new material discovery, generative design of equipment, and algorithm and software development. “The timing is perfect for EPIC,” Applied Materials’ new lab devoted to equipment and processes, he declares.
An artist’s rendering depicts Applied Materials’ new $5 billion EPIC research center, which was opened on 12 October 2026.Applied Materials
Reshaping Chip R&D, Not Just Resizing It
Physical proximity is emerging as a key advantage for chipmakers, and that is reshaping the industry’s geographic and facilities investments. The Japanese semiconductor packaging company Resonac opened its first R&D facility in the U.S. in April, for example. “These companies have a very strong reason to want to be close to their customers and close to their customers’ customers so they can make the right investments for the next five to 10 years,” according to Miller.
The knowledge of how prototype chipmaking equipment works does not move up and down the supply chain as easily as software. “The traditional way of working to get brand new technology into the hands of our customers, the chipmakers, was to ship a prototype piece of equipment from our lab into their pilot line. That’s a kind of heart-in-your-mouth type of situation,” Holtam says.
“That was always a huge point of contention,” he adds. “At what level of maturity we’re willing to allow a prototype outside of our building when the chip company is pulling on that as hard as possible.” Applied Materials analyzed 15 years of its own internal R&D to look for the places likely to benefit from fewer such heart-stopping shipments and from more shoulder-to-shoulder lab work. Then it conducted pilot programs of its customer-in-the-lab approach and got what Holtam deemed “very, very encouraging results.”
That helped prompt Applied Materials to invite top customers to set up shop inside the new EPIC lab. So far, TSMC, Samsung, Micron, Broadcom, and others have said yes. Even competing customers will get their own facilities under EPIC’s roof, with digital firewalls, physical barriers, and other security features. “We’re eliminating handoffs,” Holtam says, and making it easier for their own research staff to give customers a preview of what’s coming.
Applied Materials’ stated goal is for its EPIC center to reduce, by several years, the time it takes to go from early-stage discoveries to chip commercialization. That’s typically a 10- to 15-year process.
The U.S. Department of Commerce announced similar goals for big-tent semiconductor R&D facilities under the CHIPS Act, but those are now behind schedule or indefinitely paused. They might have helped startups get a leg up on the chip giants in a notoriously concentrated industry. Indeed, EPIC’s partnership announcements so far have been with other industry leaders, so startups may be at the back of the queue. Right now, generally, Blachier says, “small and medium companies have to cooperate with bigger companies to feed into the giants.”
Another way the industry is seeking acceleration is by closer ties with universities. Universities also serve as a bridge to the U.S. national semiconductor research strategy since universities have long-running research funding partnerships with the federal government.
“There is a benefit in having longer-term horizons and supported investments,” Blachier says, referring to EU and some Asian countries’ national chip strategies, which have created successful precompetitive research facilities such as Imec. More facilities like that in the U.S., he says, would be “definitely useful, and tend to benefit the ecosystem.”
Lucas Laursen is the technology policy editor at IEEE Spectrum. He covers how emerging technologies are changing the balance of power between companies, governments, and individuals. The rest of the time, he worries about his own balance on a bicycle, skis, or the side of a mountain.

candidato.titulo: New evidence points to two feeding black holes just 175 parsecs apart lurking in the early universe
candidato.resumo: Astronomers have found two actively feeding supermassive black holes separated by just 175 parsecs (570 light-years) in a galaxy seen when the universe was only about 2 billion years old. The system, MG B2016+112, lies at a redshift of 3.273 and is the most compact dual AGN known at this redshift. The study was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 25.

texto_fonte:
New evidence points to two feeding black holes just 175 parsecs apart lurking in the early universe
Shreejaya Karantha
Author
Astronomers have found two actively feeding supermassive black holes separated by just 175 parsecs (570 light-years) in a galaxy seen when the universe was only about 2 billion years old. The system, MG B2016+112, lies at a redshift of 3.273 and is the most compact dual AGN known at this redshift. The study was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 25.
Black hole pairs
Models predict that galaxy mergers drive gas onto central supermassive black holes, so merging galaxies should sometimes host dual active galactic nuclei (AGN). Finding close pairs is hard because of observational limitations in distinguishing nearby bright spots.
Strong gravitational lensing is useful for observing these distant objects. It occurs when a massive galaxy between the object and observer warps spacetime so strongly that the background object's light is bent and magnified, producing multiple images, arcs or rings. By magnifying distant sources, it lets astronomers reconstruct the object and study it in depth.
This study, led by Jianghao Huyan and Júlia M. Sisk-Reynés, analyzes archival VLT/MUSE spectra of MG B2016+112, a radio-loud active galaxy at redshift 3.273 that is gravitationally lensed by a foreground galaxy into three images (say A, B and C). The team explores whether the system hosts one actively feeding black hole or two. Earlier radio and X-ray studies had suggested two, about 175 parsecs (around 570 light-years) apart. The current study conducted an independent test and made new measurements using spatially resolved optical spectra of all three images.
The most compact duo
Using the archival MUSE data from 2018, they extracted spectral information for each of the three lensed images. They made corrections to remove absorption from our galaxy's gas. They also masked absorption from gas near the quasar.
Next, they measured the strengths of prominent emission lines—such as those from hydrogen, nitrogen, carbon and helium—that appeared in the three images. They found that most spectral lines were too affected by absorption to compare their ratios, but one ratio worked. The numbers matched for images A and B, while image C had a much lower value. This strongly suggested C is lit by a different black hole. "This provides strong spectroscopic evidence that C is associated with an ionizing source distinct from that producing A and B," the team writes in the paper.
They also estimated the black hole masses from the width of another line, C IV. All three estimates turned out to be in a similar mass range. The black hole associated with images A and B has an estimated mass of at least 20 to 23 million solar masses, whereas the one associated with C has an estimated mass of at least 15 million solar masses. Similar masses fit the idea of two similar galaxies having merged, each bringing its own black hole—"consistent with the interpretation that the host galaxy underwent a major merger," they explain.
Puzzling feeding pattern
The team also estimated the upper limits on the black holes' feeding rates. They found quite a difference between their feeding rates—estimates for A and B come out at about 47% and 51% of the maximum, while C is only about 4%. While this supports the dual-black-hole picture, it challenges simulations that predict the lighter black hole in a pair feeds faster: C is the lower-mass black hole and is feeding more slowly.
However, the team warns that the feeding rate for C could be uncertain, as it depends on the magnification, and the magnification they considered is only an average and may be off. The researchers call for near-infrared observations to check the masses independently.
For now, the results support the view that MG B2016+112 is a dual AGN, with images A and B from one source and image C from another. "At a projected separation of 175 pc at z = 3.273, this system represents the closest-separation confirmed dual AGN identified to date at such a high redshift," researchers conclude. The system provides a rare glimpse of black hole growth during a possible major galaxy merger in the early universe.

candidato.titulo: MIT Bengaluru Launches Quantum-Hub@MAHE With 25-Qubit System
candidato.resumo: Insider Brief PRESS RELEASE — Manipal Institute of Technology, Bengaluru (MIT Bengaluru) on Tuesday launched Manipal House of Quantum, Quantum-Hub@MAHE. Established by Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE), an Institution of Eminence Deemed to be University, the initiative will advance quantum hardware experimentation, engineering education and indigenous technology development in alignment with India’s National Quantum […]

texto_fonte:
Insider Brief
- Manipal Academy of Higher Education launched Manipal House of Quantum, Quantum-Hub@MAHE, at MIT Bengaluru to support quantum engineering, hardware experimentation and indigenous technology development in India.
- The facility begins operations with a 25-qubit open-architecture dilution refrigeration system, with plans to progress toward 150-qubit proof-of-concept platforms and industrial systems exceeding 1,000 qubits.
- Partnerships with QuantrolOx, Bluefors, Qblox and ConScience will support workforce training, hardware research and testing, while the facility aims to train 100 quantum engineers by December 2026.
PRESS RELEASE — Manipal Institute of Technology, Bengaluru (MIT Bengaluru) on Tuesday launched Manipal House of Quantum, Quantum-Hub@MAHE. Established by Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE), an Institution of Eminence Deemed to be University, the initiative will advance quantum hardware experimentation, engineering education and indigenous technology development in alignment with India’s National Quantum Mission.
The facility was inaugurated by Chief Guest Dr. Sridhar Vembu, Chief Scientist & Co-Founder, Zoho Corp, and Guest of Honour Dr. Marcus Rommel, CTO, ConScience, in the presence of Dr. Sharath K. Rao, Vice Chancellor, MAHE; Lieutenant General (Dr.) M. D. Venkatesh, VSM (Retd.), 7th Vice Chancellor, MAHE and Advisor to MEMG; Prof. (Dr.) Madhu Veeraraghavan, Pro Vice Chancellor, MAHE Bengaluru; Dr. Karunakar A. Kotegar, Pro Vice Chancellor, Technology & Science, MAHE; Dr. Raghavendra Prabhu, Additional Registrar, MAHE Bengaluru; Prof. Iven Jose, Director, MIT Bengaluru; and Mr. Vishal Chatrath, Co-Founder & CEO, QuantrolOX.
Located at the MAHE Bengaluru campus, the quantum facility at MIT Bengaluru provides students, researchers and industry collaborators with hands-on access to advanced quantum computing infrastructure, including quantum hardware, cryogenic systems and quantum control technologies. Through an integrated academic framework, the facility will support experimentation, application development, deep-tech start-up incubation, component innovation, testing and translational research, positioning MIT Bengaluru as an emerging centre for quantum engineering and indigenous hardware development.
The facility commences operations with a 25-qubit open-architecture dilution refrigeration system designed for advanced training and experimentation. This marks the first phase of a structured roadmap progressing from sub-50-qubit training systems to 150-qubit proof-of-concept platforms and, ultimately, to industrial-grade quantum product systems with more than 1,000 qubits.
Speaking at the inauguration, Dr. Sridhar Vembu, Chief Scientist & Co-Founder, Zoho Corp, said, “Q-HUB is a place for students to dream, think deeply and turn their ideas into conviction and action. Just as personal computers and the internet transformed possibilities for my generation, quantum computing can empower this generation to build new machines, create breakthrough applications and take India to greater heights.”
Highlighting MAHE’s commitment to emerging technologies, Dr. Sharath K. Rao, Vice Chancellor, MAHE, said, “The MAHE House of Quantum at MIT Bengaluru reflects MAHE’s commitment to building advanced scientific capabilities and nurturing talent in emerging technologies. By creating access to modern quantum infrastructure, we aim to contribute meaningfully to India’s growing quantum ecosystem.”
Prof. (Dr.) Madhu Veeraraghavan, Pro Vice Chancellor, MAHE Bengaluru, said, “The Hub brings together education, research and innovation on a common platform. It will create opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and help translate academic research into real-world technological impact.”
Prof. Iven Jose, Director, MIT Bengaluru, said, “The quantum facility at MIT Bengaluru will provide students and researchers with valuable exposure to real quantum systems and engineering environments. It marks an important step towards developing the next generation of quantum scientists, engineers and innovators.”
Ahead of the launch, faculty members and students from the Bengaluru and Manipal campuses completed specialised training at the MIT Bengaluru campus and the QuantrolOx laboratory at QuTech, TU Delft, in the Netherlands. The programme developed practical capabilities in dilution refrigerator assembly, cryogenic systems, quantum control technologies, QPU measurements and superconducting quantum hardware, preparing the team to support the operations of the quantum facility at MIT Bengaluru.
The facility will support learning and research in areas such as healthcare, pharmaceuticals, oncology, aerospace and advanced computing. It will also strengthen MIT Bengaluru’s collaboration with industry and research organisations while developing a future-ready talent pipeline in quantum technologies.
The initiative has been formalised through Memorandums of Agreement with QuantrolOx of Finland, in association with Bluefors of Finland, Qblox of the Netherlands and ConScience of Sweden. These collaborations establish a first-year roadmap focused on workforce development, hardware experimentation, intellectual property co-development and national testing infrastructure.
As part of its workforce development efforts, the quantum facility at MIT Bengaluru aims to train 100 quantum engineers by December 2026. It will also conduct quantum awareness programmes, summer and winter camps for Class 10 and Class 12 students across rural India, short hands-on exposure programmes and capacity-building initiatives for technical professionals.
The facility will provide researchers, start-ups and industry partners with access to advanced quantum testing and measurement infrastructure, strengthening interdisciplinary collaboration, innovation and India’s growing quantum technology ecosystem.

texto_fonte:
In an age of 4TB SSDs and massive NVMe drives, many users tend to leave the entire storage space as a single, huge system drive. While this is convenient, from an administrative point of view it is a risky move that amounts to flying blind. Instead, we recommend strategically partitioning your largest drives.
This brings tangible benefits for data security, system recovery, and backup efficiency. Think of partitions as digital firewalls within your hardware. If your operating system becomes corrupted by a faulty driver, a failed update, or even malware, a clean reinstallation is often the quickest way back to a stable system.
However, if you’ve stored everything on a single partition, you’ll have to laboriously back up terabytes of data before reinstalling, or risk losing it when formatting the drive.
By separating the operating system onto partition C: and your user data onto partition D:, you can completely wipe and reinstall Windows, while your game collections, video projects, and documents on the second partition remain completely untouched. This not only saves time but also spares you a lot of stress in crisis situations.
Kingston
To implement this optimization, you must first analyze your current configuration. To do this, open the Command Prompt with administrator rights and enter the command fsutil fsinfo ntfsinfo C:, then press the Enter key to confirm. Look for the value ‘Bytes per cluster’ in the results.
By default, Windows uses 4KB, which is ideal for the system partition to minimize fragmentation when dealing with many small system files. However, for data-only partitions where you mainly store large files such as 4K videos or backups, it makes sense to adjust the cluster size to 64KB.
Here’s how to do it: The neatest way to change the cluster size in Windows 11 is via Windows Settings. Press the Windows + I key combination to open Settings. In the left-hand menu, navigate to ‘System’ and then click on ‘Storage’ on the right. Scroll down to the ‘Storage management’ section.
Foundry
Next, expand ‘Advanced storage settings’ and select ‘Disks and volumes.’ A list of all physical drives will appear. Click the arrow next to your hard drive to view the associated partitions (volumes). Select the desired data partition and click the ‘Properties’ button.
Next, click the ‘Format’ button. The crucial dialog box will now open. Here, under ‘Label,’ enter a name for your drive. Ensure that ‘NTFS’ is selected under ‘File system.’ In the ‘Allocation unit size’ drop-down menu, select ‘64KB’ explicitly instead of ‘Standard (4KB).’
Tick the box next to ‘Perform quick format’ and confirm the process by clicking ‘Format.’ Please note: This process will irrevocably delete all data on this partition. You should therefore only carry it out on newly created or empty data partitions.
Foundry
This adjustment to 64KB is so effective because it reduces fragmentation in large files and minimizes the amount of metadata that needs to be managed in the Master File Table (MFT). Please bear in mind a technical limitation: With the standard cluster size of 4KB, an NTFS partition is limited to a maximum of 16TB.
If you upgrade to even larger drives in future, you must use larger clusters to be able to utilize the full capacity. On modern SSDs, you should also ensure that the partitions are aligned with the internal NAND memory.
Nowadays, Windows handles this correctly and automatically when creating partitions via Disk Management or the Settings app, in order to avoid unnecessary write cycles (write amplification).

texto_fonte:
IA mais poderosa do Google, Gemini 4 Argon chega para assinantes Pro e Ultra na web
Por Viviane França |
O Google liberou, nesta terça-feira (13),o Gemini 4 Argon para assinantes dos planos Google AI Pro e AI Ultra. Descrito pela empresa como seu modelo de inteligência artificial mais poderoso até o momento, ele está disponível no aplicativo Gemini e na versão web, com melhorias em raciocínio, programação e execução autônoma de tarefas.
Antes restrito a um grupo menor de usuários, o modelo passou por ajustes de segurança contra jailbreaks, tentativas de contornar as proteções da IA. A versão pública também apresenta respostas mais objetivas, com menos repetições e frases genéricas, além de atualizações frequentes sobre o andamento de tarefas demoradas.
Quais são as novidades do Gemini 4 Argon?
Um dos destaques é a integração com mais de 40 aplicativos, como Instacart, OpenTable, Adobe e Shopify. O sistema pode executar atividades, como compras de supermercado, reservas em restaurantes e trabalhos de design, inclusive sem que o usuário precise acompanhar cada etapa diante do computador.
O modelo ainda recebeu melhorias na comunicação, com respostas diretas e menos hesitação, além de atualizações sobre o progresso de operações longas. A proposta é tornar as interações mais claras e facilitar o acompanhamento de tarefas complexas.
Além de responder a perguntas, o Gemini pode assumir atividades que envolvem diferentes etapas e serviços. Para isso, o usuário pode alternar entre o bate-papo convencional e o modo de tarefas por meio de um botão na janela principal do chat. Nesse segundo modo, a IA executa ações de forma autônoma e se conecta a dezenas de aplicativos, conforme as instruções recebidas e os recursos disponíveis em cada plataforma.
Na programação, os avanços incluem melhorias na geração de código e a integração do Google Antigravity ao aplicativo Gemini para macOS.

candidato.titulo: Nova usina solar com hidrogênio chinesa "ligaria" capital brasileira por 37 dias
candidato.resumo: Uma nova etapa do maior complexo integrado de energia solar, baterias e hidrogênio da China entrou em operação nesta quarta-feira (14). Instalado em Rudong, na província costeira de Jiangsu, o projeto é tão grande que sua produção anual de eletricidade seria equivalente a aproximadamente 37 dias de todo o consumo de uma capital brasileira como Curitiba . Isso não significa que a instalação conseguiria manter a capital paranaense literalmente ligada durante 37 dias consecutivos. A comparação considera apenas o volume de energia produzido ao longo de um ano pela parte fotovoltaica do complexo e o consumo médio diário de Curitiba. Há limitações de potência, armazenamento e, obviamente, distância entre os dois lugares. O complexo de Guohua Rudong reúne 400 MW de geração fotovoltaica , uma estação de baterias com potência de 60 MW e capacidade de 120 MWh e uma instalação capaz de produzir até 1.500 metros cúbicos padrão de hidrogênio por hora. Há ainda uma subestação de 220 kV responsável pela integração do projeto à rede elétrica. texto_fonte:
Nova usina solar com hidrogênio chinesa "ligaria" capital brasileira por 37 dias
Por Léo Müller |
Uma nova etapa do maior complexo integrado de energia solar, baterias e hidrogênio da China entrou em operação nesta quarta-feira (14). Instalado em Rudong, na província costeira de Jiangsu, o projeto é tão grande que sua produção anual de eletricidade seria equivalente a aproximadamente 37 dias de todo o consumo de uma capital brasileira como Curitiba.
Isso não significa que a instalação conseguiria manter a capital paranaense literalmente ligada durante 37 dias consecutivos. A comparação considera apenas o volume de energia produzido ao longo de um ano pela parte fotovoltaica do complexo e o consumo médio diário de Curitiba. Há limitações de potência, armazenamento e, obviamente, distância entre os dois lugares.
O complexo de Guohua Rudong reúne 400 MW de geração fotovoltaica, uma estação de baterias com potência de 60 MW e capacidade de 120 MWh e uma instalação capaz de produzir até 1.500 metros cúbicos padrão de hidrogênio por hora. Há ainda uma subestação de 220 kV responsável pela integração do projeto à rede elétrica.
Hidrogênio resolve ponto fraco da energia solar
A ideia é aproveitar melhor uma das maiores limitações da energia solar: o fato de sua produção variar bastante durante o dia.
Quando os painéis estiverem gerando mais eletricidade do que a rede consegue absorver, parte desse excedente pode ser armazenada nas baterias ou utilizada para produzir hidrogênio verde por eletrólise da água. A bateria pode devolver eletricidade à rede ou abastecer a própria instalação quando necessário, enquanto o hidrogênio passa a ser outro produto energético do complexo.
Segundo o governo chinês, a instalação tem capacidade para produzir 482 toneladas de hidrogênio verde por ano, destinado principalmente ao mercado da região do delta do rio Yangtzé. A integração ajuda a evitar que parte da geração renovável seja simplesmente desperdiçada em períodos de excesso de oferta.
Energia equivalente a 37 dias de Curitiba
Para colocar a escala do projeto em perspectiva, o Canaltech comparou sua produção anual estimada com o consumo de eletricidade de Curitiba.
A usina de Rudong deve gerar cerca de 468 milhões de kWh por ano. Para efeito de comparação, Curitiba consumiu aproximadamente 4,64 bilhões de kWh em 2023, segundo dados da Copel e do IPARDES divulgados pela Prefeitura. Isso equivale a uma média de 12,72 milhões de kWh por dia na capital paranaense. Dessa forma, a produção anual prevista do complexo chinês corresponde a cerca de 37 dias do consumo de eletricidade de Curitiba.
Os 468 GWh representam cerca de 10,1% de tudo o que a capital paranaense consumiu em 2023. Fazendo uma conta parecida com essa, podemos dizer que a mesma usina geraria energia suficiente para 6 dias a cidade de São Paulo, ou 11 dias para a cidade do Rio de Janeiro.
Apesar de produzir muita energia, a usina não conseguiria sozinha "manter ligada" nenhuma dessas três cidades brasileiras, já que todas elas demandam mais energia em média do que ela consegue gerar no dia.
Hidrogênio não é exatamente uma bateria neste projeto
O complexo consegue usar eletricidade renovável para produzir hidrogênio, que pode ser armazenado por períodos muito maiores do que a energia guardada em uma bateria convencional. Em teoria, esse hidrogênio também poderia voltar a ser convertido em eletricidade em outro equipamento.
Mas essa não é a principal função anunciada para o hidrogênio produzido em Rudong. O governo chinês informa que o combustível será direcionado principalmente para consumo na região do delta do rio Yangtzé. A estação eletroquímica de 60 MW/120 MWh é que funciona efetivamente como bateria da usina, suavizando as variações da geração solar e ajudando a deslocar energia entre períodos de maior e menor produção.
Em outra descrição oficial do projeto, as autoridades explicam que, quando há bastante sol, a eletricidade verde é priorizada para a rede e o excedente pode alimentar armazenamento e produção de hidrogênio. Em momentos de menor geração, a bateria ajuda a equilibrar o sistema.
Usina solar já funcionava antes
Apesar de a notícia desta quarta tratar da entrada em operação da estação de armazenamento, o projeto não começou a gerar eletricidade agora.
Os primeiros módulos foram conectados ainda no fim de 2024, e os 400 MW de painéis solares atingiram conexão integral à rede em 29 de abril de 2025. Na ocasião, autoridades locais já estimavam uma geração anual média de aproximadamente 468 GWh.
O complexo integrado foi declarado totalmente construído pelo governo chinês em 10 de junho de 2026, com geração solar, baterias e produção de hidrogênio reunidas no mesmo projeto. A novidade agora é a entrada formal em operação da estação de armazenamento divulgada nesta quarta-feira.
Além de ajudar a estabilizar a geração renovável, o governo chinês estima que o projeto possa evitar a emissão de mais de 300 mil toneladas de CO₂ por ano.

candidato.titulo: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
candidato.resumo: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.

texto_fonte:
The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.
On October 8, the U.K. issued sanctions (PDF) against Cryptomus — previously known as Certa Payments and Xeltox Enterprises — for processing payments that benefit the Russian government and its financial institutions. The sanctions freeze any Cryptomus assets at U.K. banks, and bar British companies from offering it any business, virtual or otherwise. Also targeted in these sanctions were the virtual payment platforms VexPay, TokenSpot, and the Tsunami Payments service.
As explained in our December 2024 investigation, “How Cryptocurrency Turns to Cash in Russian Banks,” Cryptomus has been a key payment processor for dozens of Russian cryptocurrency exchanges and websites hawking cybercrime services. The company has changed its name several times since emerging in 2022, most recently to “Heleket” last year after Canada levied a record CAD $176 million fine against the platform for anti-money laundering violations.
The blockchain data-crunching firm Chainalysis said the U.K. sanctions target the broader infrastructure supporting Russia’s wartime economy.
“Cryptomus and Heleket have emerged as major payment hubs for illicit activity,” Chainalysis wrote in an October 8 blog post. “Together, these services received more illicit funds across tracked categories than the mixers in our dataset and the number of illicit counterparties surged to more than 900 in a single month in late 2025.”
In April 2026, the blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs found Cryptomus had processed more than $7 billion in transactions since its inception in 2022, including transactions associated with child sexual abuse material vendors, terrorist financing networks, and human trafficking operations.
TRM noted that Cryptomus’s transaction volume cratered after the platform instituted new “know your customer” or KYC rules, and that the cryptocurrency platform responded to the Canadian fines by launching Heleket as a parallel service that continued to offer no-KYC payment processing.
Richard Sanders is a blockchain analyst and investigator who spent months mapping out Cryptomus’s payment infrastructure and transacting with its customers. Sanders said the U.K. sanctions on Cryptomus are important because Canada’s sanctions against the platform were ultimately unenforceable and uncollectible.
“A fine doesn’t stop a cryptocurrency payment processor from processing payments,” Sanders wrote on LinkedIn. “Sanctions kill the operation. The distinction matters.”
As our 2024 investigation noted, Cryptomus shared a Vancouver address with dozens of other foreign currency dealers and money transfer businesses — none of which appeared to be physically located there. Following the CAD $176 million fine for alleged money laundering violations, Cryptomus appealed the penalty, launched Heleket as a parallel service, and kept on processing large volumes of sketchy transactions, Sanders said.
Sanders said the sanctions also are notable because they are the first known instance of a “Five Eyes” country (referring to the Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the U.K. and the U.S.) sanctioning a cryptocurrency operation incorporated in another Five Eyes jurisdiction.
Where do entities like Cryptomus and Heleket derive their authority to offer international financial services? The answer appears to involve fake financial institutions overseen by a phony regulatory body positioned in a country that is not widely recognized as a sovereign nation.
Our 2024 investigation found the sole shareholder of Cryptomus’s parent company Certa Payments was a 25-year-old Ukrainian woman who also headed several other firms, including the WS Management and Advisory Corporation, which bills itself as the regulatory body that exclusively oversees licenses for cryptocurrency, foreign exchange and online gaming businesses incorporated in the disputed region in northwest Africa known as the Western Sahara.
That entity’s website — crasadr.com — says it assists applicants with bank setup and formation, online gaming licenses, and the creation and licensing of foreign exchange brokers. One of Certa Payments’ former sites — certa[.]website — also shared a server with 12 other domains, including rasd-state[.]ws, a website for the Central Reserve Authority of the Western Sahara.
